ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Hooks allow functional components to utilize state and lifecycle features without writing class components.
Rules of Hooks:
1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.
2. Only call Hooks from React function components or custom Hooks.

USESTATE HOOK:
`const [state, setState] = useState(initialValue);`

metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.title: PostgreSQL Database Design
metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.title: JavaScript ES6+ Deep Dive
metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.
3.

Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.title: JavaScript ES6+ Deep Dive
metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.
3.

metadata.title: React Hooks Tutorial
metadata.heading: REACT HOOKS OVERVIEW & RULES
metadata.content:
REACT HOOKS OVERVIEW & RULES:
Hooks allow functional components to utilize state and lifecycle features without writing class components.
Rules of Hooks:
1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.
2. Only call Hooks from React function components or custom Hooks.

USESTATE HOOK:
`const [state, setState] = useState(initialValue);`

metadata.heading: CSS GRID SYSTEM
metadata.content:

- grid-template-columns: Defines track sizes for columns (e.g., repeat(3, 1fr) creates 3 equal columns; repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr)) creates responsive fluid columns without media queries).

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.title: PostgreSQL Database Design
metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Hooks allow functional components to utilize state and lifecycle features without writing class components.
Rules of Hooks:
1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.
2. Only call Hooks from React function components or custom Hooks.

USESTATE HOOK:
`const [state, setState] = useState(initialValue);`

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Rules of Hooks:
1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.
2. Only call Hooks from React function components or custom Hooks.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.content:

- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: USEEFFECT HOOK
metadata.content:
USEEFFECT HOOK:
- No dependency array `useEffect(() => {})`: Runs after EVERY render.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.
3.

metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: USEEFFECT HOOK
metadata.content:
USEEFFECT HOOK:
- No dependency array `useEffect(() => {})`: Runs after EVERY render.
- Empty array `useEffect(() => {}, [])`: Runs ONCE after initial mount.
- With dependencies `useEffect(() => {}, [userId])`: Runs after mount and when any dependency value changes by shallow comparison (Object.is).

metadata.content:

- Libuv provides a thread pool (default 4 worker threads) to handle non-blocking asynchronous I/O operations like file system reads, DNS lookups, and crypto hashing.

metadata.heading: ACID TRANSACTIONS
metadata.content:
ACID TRANSACTIONS:
- Consistency: Data transitions from one valid state to another, respecting all constraints, foreign keys, and triggers.
- Isolation: Concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other. Isolation levels: Read Uncommitted, Read Committed (Postgres default), Repeatable Read, Serializable.

metadata.title: PostgreSQL Database Design
metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.title: React Hooks Tutorial
metadata.heading: USEEFFECT HOOK
metadata.content:
USEEFFECT HOOK:
- No dependency array `useEffect(() => {})`: Runs after EVERY render.
- Empty array `useEffect(() => {}, [])`: Runs ONCE after initial mount.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

Stored by placing a UNIQUE foreign key in one of the tables.

- Many-to-Many (M:N): e.g., Students to Batches. Requires a junction (associative) table with composite primary key or foreign keys (student_batches table with student_id and batch_id).

metadata.title: React Hooks Tutorial
metadata.heading: REACT HOOKS OVERVIEW & RULES
metadata.content:
REACT HOOKS OVERVIEW & RULES:
Hooks allow functional components to utilize state and lifecycle features without writing class components.
Rules of Hooks:
1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.
2. Only call Hooks from React function components or custom Hooks.

USESTATE HOOK:
`const [state, setState] = useState(initialValue);`

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:

- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Libuv provides a thread pool (default 4 worker threads) to handle non-blocking asynchronous I/O operations like file system reads, DNS lookups, and crypto hashing.

metadata.heading: RELATIONAL DATABASE MODELING
metadata.content:
RELATIONAL DATABASE MODELING:
Stored by placing a UNIQUE foreign key in one of the tables.
- One-to-Many (1:N): e.g., Course to Batches. Foreign key is placed in the child table (batches table has course_id references courses(id)).
- Many-to-Many (M:N): e.g., Students to Batches. Requires a junction (associative) table with composite primary key or foreign keys (student_batches table with student_id and batch_id).

Normalization eliminates data redundancy and prevents insertion, update, and deletion anomalies.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.content:

- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.content:

Hooks allow functional components to utilize state and lifecycle features without writing class components.
Rules of Hooks:
1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.
2. Only call Hooks from React function components or custom Hooks.

USESTATE HOOK:
`const [state, setState] = useState(initialValue);`

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.content:

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: REACT HOOKS OVERVIEW & RULES
metadata.content:
REACT HOOKS OVERVIEW & RULES:
Hooks allow functional components to utilize state and lifecycle features without writing class components.
Rules of Hooks:
1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.
2. Only call Hooks from React function components or custom Hooks.

USESTATE HOOK:
`const [state, setState] = useState(initialValue);`

metadata.content:
RELATIONAL DATABASE MODELING:
Stored by placing a UNIQUE foreign key in one of the tables.
- One-to-Many (1:N): e.g., Course to Batches. Foreign key is placed in the child table (batches table has course_id references courses(id)).
- Many-to-Many (M:N): e.g., Students to Batches. Requires a junction (associative) table with composite primary key or foreign keys (student_batches table with student_id and batch_id).

DATABASE NORMALIZATION FORMS:
Normalization eliminates data redundancy and prevents insertion, update, and deletion anomalies.

metadata.heading: USEEFFECT HOOK
metadata.content:

- No dependency array `useEffect(() => {})`: Runs after EVERY render.
- Empty array `useEffect(() => {}, [])`: Runs ONCE after initial mount.
- With dependencies `useEffect(() => {}, [userId])`: Runs after mount and when any dependency value changes by shallow comparison (Object.is).

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: RELATIONAL DATABASE MODELING
metadata.content:
RELATIONAL DATABASE MODELING:
Stored by placing a UNIQUE foreign key in one of the tables.
- One-to-Many (1:N): e.g., Course to Batches. Foreign key is placed in the child table (batches table has course_id references courses(id)).
- Many-to-Many (M:N): e.g., Students to Batches. Requires a junction (associative) table with composite primary key or foreign keys (student_batches table with student_id and batch_id).

1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Rules of Hooks:
1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.
2. Only call Hooks from React function components or custom Hooks.

USESTATE HOOK:

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.
3.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Stored by placing a UNIQUE foreign key in one of the tables.

- Many-to-Many (M:N): e.g., Students to Batches. Requires a junction (associative) table with composite primary key or foreign keys (student_batches table with student_id and batch_id).

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.
3.

1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.

metadata.content:

Hooks allow functional components to utilize state and lifecycle features without writing class components.
Rules of Hooks:
1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.
2. Only call Hooks from React function components or custom Hooks.

USESTATE HOOK:
`const [state, setState] = useState(initialValue);`

1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: RELATIONAL DATABASE MODELING

RELATIONAL DATABASE MODELING:
Stored by placing a UNIQUE foreign key in one of the tables.
- One-to-Many (1:N): e.g., Course to Batches. Foreign key is placed in the child table (batches table has course_id references courses(id)).
- Many-to-Many (M:N): e.g., Students to Batches. Requires a junction (associative) table with composite primary key or foreign keys (student_batches table with student_id and batch_id).

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.
3.

metadata.title: React Hooks Tutorial
metadata.heading: REACT HOOKS OVERVIEW & RULES
metadata.content:
REACT HOOKS OVERVIEW & RULES:
Hooks allow functional components to utilize state and lifecycle features without writing class components.
Rules of Hooks:
1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.
2. Only call Hooks from React function components or custom Hooks.

USESTATE HOOK:
`const [state, setState] = useState(initialValue);`

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.title: PostgreSQL Database Design
metadata.heading: ACID TRANSACTIONS
metadata.content:
ACID TRANSACTIONS:
- Consistency: Data transitions from one valid state to another, respecting all constraints, foreign keys, and triggers.
- Isolation: Concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other. Isolation levels: Read Uncommitted, Read Committed (Postgres default), Repeatable Read, Serializable.

metadata.title: PostgreSQL Database Design
metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.content:

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.content:
NODE.JS ARCHITECTURE & EVENT LOOP:
- Libuv provides a thread pool (default 4 worker threads) to handle non-blocking asynchronous I/O operations like file system reads, DNS lookups, and crypto hashing.
- The Event Loop continuously checks phases: Timers (setTimeout) -> Pending Callbacks -> Idle/Prepare -> Poll (I/O) -> Check (setImmediate) -> Close Callbacks.

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:

- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.content:
USEEFFECT HOOK:
- No dependency array `useEffect(() => {})`: Runs after EVERY render.
- Empty array `useEffect(() => {}, [])`: Runs ONCE after initial mount.
- With dependencies `useEffect(() => {}, [userId])`: Runs after mount and when any dependency value changes by shallow comparison (Object.is).

metadata.heading: NODE.JS ARCHITECTURE & EVENT LOOP
metadata.content:
NODE.JS ARCHITECTURE & EVENT LOOP:
- Libuv provides a thread pool (default 4 worker threads) to handle non-blocking asynchronous I/O operations like file system reads, DNS lookups, and crypto hashing.
- The Event Loop continuously checks phases: Timers (setTimeout) -> Pending Callbacks -> Idle/Prepare -> Poll (I/O) -> Check (setImmediate) -> Close Callbacks.

metadata.title: PostgreSQL Database Design
metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.
3.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.content:

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Stored by placing a UNIQUE foreign key in one of the tables.

metadata.content:

- Consistency: Data transitions from one valid state to another, respecting all constraints, foreign keys, and triggers.
- Isolation: Concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other. Isolation levels: Read Uncommitted, Read Committed (Postgres default), Repeatable Read, Serializable.

metadata.title: PostgreSQL Database Design
metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.title: React Hooks Tutorial
metadata.heading: REACT HOOKS OVERVIEW & RULES
metadata.content:
REACT HOOKS OVERVIEW & RULES:
Hooks allow functional components to utilize state and lifecycle features without writing class components.
Rules of Hooks:

1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.title: PostgreSQL Database Design
metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.
3.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.
3.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`

1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.content:

Hooks allow functional components to utilize state and lifecycle features without writing class components.
Rules of Hooks:
1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.
2. Only call Hooks from React function components or custom Hooks.

USESTATE HOOK:
`const [state, setState] = useState(initialValue);`

metadata.title: PostgreSQL Database Design
metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.title: PostgreSQL Database Design
metadata.heading: RELATIONAL DATABASE MODELING
metadata.content:
RELATIONAL DATABASE MODELING:
Stored by placing a UNIQUE foreign key in one of the tables.
- One-to-Many (1:N): e.g., Course to Batches. Foreign key is placed in the child table (batches table has course_id references courses(id)).
- Many-to-Many (M:N): e.g., Students to Batches. Requires a junction (associative) table with composite primary key or foreign keys (student_batches table with student_id and batch_id).

DATABASE NORMALIZATION FORMS:

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.
3.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

Stored by placing a UNIQUE foreign key in one of the tables.

- Many-to-Many (M:N): e.g., Students to Batches. Requires a junction (associative) table with composite primary key or foreign keys (student_batches table with student_id and batch_id).

- Many-to-Many (M:N): e.g., Students to Batches. Requires a junction (associative) table with composite primary key or foreign keys (student_batches table with student_id and batch_id).

metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.content:

- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.content:

metadata.content:
NODE.JS ARCHITECTURE & EVENT LOOP:
- Libuv provides a thread pool (default 4 worker threads) to handle non-blocking asynchronous I/O operations like file system reads, DNS lookups, and crypto hashing.
- The Event Loop continuously checks phases: Timers (setTimeout) -> Pending Callbacks -> Idle/Prepare -> Poll (I/O) -> Check (setImmediate) -> Close Callbacks.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: REACT HOOKS OVERVIEW & RULES
metadata.content:
REACT HOOKS OVERVIEW & RULES:
Hooks allow functional components to utilize state and lifecycle features without writing class components.
Rules of Hooks:
1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.
2. Only call Hooks from React function components or custom Hooks.

USESTATE HOOK:
`const [state, setState] = useState(initialValue);`

- Many-to-Many (M:N): e.g., Students to Batches. Requires a junction (associative) table with composite primary key or foreign keys (student_batches table with student_id and batch_id).

metadata.title: PostgreSQL Database Design
metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.title: PostgreSQL Database Design
metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.title: PostgreSQL Database Design
metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.content:
RELATIONAL DATABASE MODELING:

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.content:

- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.title: PostgreSQL Database Design
metadata.heading: ACID TRANSACTIONS
metadata.content:
ACID TRANSACTIONS:
- Consistency: Data transitions from one valid state to another, respecting all constraints, foreign keys, and triggers.
- Isolation: Concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other. Isolation levels: Read Uncommitted, Read Committed (Postgres default), Repeatable Read, Serializable.

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.content:

- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.title: JavaScript ES6+ Deep Dive
metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.
3.

1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.
3.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

metadata.heading: REACT HOOKS OVERVIEW & RULES
metadata.content:
REACT HOOKS OVERVIEW & RULES:
Hooks allow functional components to utilize state and lifecycle features without writing class components.
Rules of Hooks:
1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.
2. Only call Hooks from React function components or custom Hooks.

USESTATE HOOK:
`const [state, setState] = useState(initialValue);`

metadata.heading: CSS GRID SYSTEM
metadata.content:
CSS GRID SYSTEM:
- grid-template-columns: Defines track sizes for columns (e.g., repeat(3, 1fr) creates 3 equal columns; repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr)) creates responsive fluid columns without media queries).
- grid-template-rows: Defines track sizes for rows.
- gap: Sets spacing between grid cells (e.g., gap: 24px).
- grid-column / grid-row: Specifies an item's start and end line positions (e.g., grid-column: span 2 spans across two columns).

1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`

1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.content:

Stored by placing a UNIQUE foreign key in one of the tables.

- Many-to-Many (M:N): e.g., Students to Batches. Requires a junction (associative) table with composite primary key or foreign keys (student_batches table with student_id and batch_id).

metadata.title: React Hooks Tutorial
metadata.heading: USEEFFECT HOOK
metadata.content:
USEEFFECT HOOK:
- No dependency array `useEffect(() => {})`: Runs after EVERY render.
- Empty array `useEffect(() => {}, [])`: Runs ONCE after initial mount.
- With dependencies `useEffect(() => {}, [userId])`: Runs after mount and when any dependency value changes by shallow comparison (Object.is).

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.
3.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

REACT HOOKS OVERVIEW & RULES:
Hooks allow functional components to utilize state and lifecycle features without writing class components.
Rules of Hooks:
1. Only call Hooks at the top level of your component. Do not call Hooks inside loops, conditions, or nested functions.
2. Only call Hooks from React function components or custom Hooks.

USESTATE HOOK:
`const [state, setState] = useState(initialValue);`

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE
metadata.content:
INDEXING STRATEGIES & PERFORMANCE:
- Composite Index: Indexes multiple columns together. Column order matters (Leftmost prefix rule: an index on (course_id, date) supports queries on course_id alone, but not date alone).
- Inverted/GIN Index: Used for JSONB, full-text search, and array containment.
- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

- Vector Index (IVFFlat/HNSW): Used in pgvector for high-dimensional approximate nearest neighbor searches using cosine or L2 distance.

1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

metadata.heading: ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS
metadata.content:
ARROW FUNCTIONS & LEXICAL THIS:
Arrow functions provide concise syntax: `const add = (a, b) => a + b;`
Key differences from regular functions:
1. Lexical `this`: Arrow functions do not bind their own `this`; they inherit `this` from the enclosing lexical execution context. This eliminates the need for `.bind(this)` or `const self = this` in callbacks.
2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.

2. No `arguments` object: Use rest parameters `(...args)` instead.
